sanskrit: koṭīśatavṛtau cāpi gajo gavaya eva ca vānarendrau mahāvīryau pṛthak pṛthag adṛśyatām
english: And the two mighty monkey-lords Gaja and Gavaya, each surrounded by a hundred crore warriors, were seen separately from one another.

sanskrit: ṣaṣṭikoṭisahasrāṇi prakarṣan pratyadṛśyata golāṅgūlo mahārāja gavākṣo bhīmadarśanaḥ
english: O great king, the fearsome Golāṅgūla and Gavākṣa were seen leading sixty thousand crore troops.

sanskrit: gandhamādanavāsī tu prathito gandhamādanaḥ koṭīsahasram ugrāṇāṃ harīṇāṃ samakarṣata
english: The celebrated Gandhamādana, dweller of the Gandhamādana mountain, gathered a thousand crore fierce monkeys.

sanskrit: panaso nāma medhāvī vānaraḥ sumahābalaḥ koṭīr daśa dvādaśa ca triṃśatpañca prakarṣati
english: A monkey named Panasa, wise and of immense strength, led ten, twelve, and thirty-five crore troops.

sanskrit: śrīmān dadhimukho nāma harivṛddho 'pi vīryavān pracakarṣa mahat sainyaṃ harīṇāṃ bhīmatejasām
english: The illustrious Dadhimukha, an aged monkey yet full of valor, led a vast army of monkeys possessed of terrible energy.

sanskrit: kṛṣṇānāṃ mukhapuṇḍrāṇām ṛkṣāṇāṃ bhīmakarmaṇām koṭīśatasahasreṇa jāmbavān pratyadṛśyata
english: Jāmbavān was seen with a hundred thousand crore of bears — dark ones with face-markings, doers of terrible deeds.

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo hariyūthapayūthapāḥ asaṃkhyeyā mahārāja samīyū rāmakāraṇāt
english: These and many other leaders of monkey troops, innumerable, O great king, came together for the sake of Rāma.

sanskrit: śirīṣakusumābhānāṃ siṃhānām iva nardatām śrūyate tumulaḥ śabdas tatra tatra pradhāvatām
english: A tumultuous sound was heard everywhere of those rushing about — roaring like lions, radiant as shirisha blossoms.

sanskrit: girikūṭanibhāḥ ke cit ke cin mahiṣasaṃnibhāḥ śaradabhrapratīkāśāḥ piṣṭahiṅgulakānanāḥ
english: Some were like mountain peaks, some resembled great buffaloes, some shone like autumnal clouds, some had complexions red as powdered vermillion.

sanskrit: utpatantaḥ patantaś ca plavamānāś ca vānarāḥ uddhunvanto 'pare reṇūn samājagmuḥ samantataḥ
english: Monkeys leaping up, falling down, and bounding forward, while others raised clouds of dust, came together from all directions.

sanskrit: sa vānaramahālokaḥ pūrṇasāgarasaṃnibhaḥ niveśam akarot tatra sugrīvānumate tadā
english: That vast multitude of monkeys, resembling the full ocean, made camp there at that time by Sugrīva's command.

sanskrit: tatas teṣu harīndreṣu samāvṛtteṣu sarvaśaḥ tithau praśaste nakṣatre muhūrte cābhipūjite
english: Then, when all the monkey chiefs had assembled on every side, on an auspicious lunar day, under a favorable asterism, at a well-honored muhurta,

sanskrit: tena vyūḍhena sainyena lokān udvartayann iva prayayau rāghavaḥ śrīmān sugrīvasahitas tadā
english: the illustrious Rāghava set forth with Sugrīva, leading that arrayed army as if to turn the worlds upside down.

sanskrit: mukham āsīt tu sainyasya hanūmān mārutātmajaḥ jaghanaṃ pālayām āsa saumitrir akutobhayaḥ
english: Hanūmān, son of the Wind-god, led the van of the army, while Lakṣmaṇa, son of Sumitrā, fearless of all, guarded the rear.

sanskrit: baddhagodhāṅgulitrāṇau rāghavau tatra rejatuḥ vṛtau harimahāmātraiś candrasūryau grahair iva
english: The two Rāghavas, with leather finger-guards strapped on, shone there surrounded by the great monkey chiefs, like the moon and sun surrounded by planets.

sanskrit: prababhau harisainyaṃ tac chālatālaśilāyudham sumahac chālibhavanaṃ yathā sūryodayaṃ prati
english: That monkey army, armed with sala trees, palm trees, and rocks, shone brilliantly like a vast field of rice at sunrise.

sanskrit: nalanīlāṅgadakrāthamaindadvividapālitā yayau sumahatī senā rāghavasyārthasiddhaye
english: That great army, protected by Nala, Nīla, Aṅgada, Krātha, Mainda, and Dvivida, marched forth for the accomplishment of Rāghava's purpose.

sanskrit: vidhivat supraśasteṣu bahumūlaphaleṣu ca prabhūtamadhumāṃseṣu vārimatsu śiveṣu ca
english: Halting duly at duly auspicious places abounding in roots and fruits, rich in honey and meat, with water and pleasant surroundings,

sanskrit: nivasantī nirābādhā tathaiva girisānuṣu upāyād dharisenā sā kṣārodam atha sāgaram
english: staying without disturbance on mountain slopes as well, that monkey army at last reached the salt sea, the ocean.

sanskrit: dvitīyasāgaranibhaṃ tad balaṃ bahuladhvajam velāvanaṃ samāsādya nivāsam akarot tadā
english: That army, like a second ocean, with its many banners, upon reaching the seashore forest, made camp there.

sanskrit: tato dāśarathiḥ śrīmān sugrīvaṃ pratyabhāṣata madhye vānaramukhyānāṃ prāptakālam idaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then the illustrious son of Daśaratha spoke to Sugrīva in the midst of the monkey chiefs, saying these timely words:

sanskrit: upāyaḥ ko nu bhavatāṃ mataḥ sāgaralaṅghane iyaṃ ca mahatī senā sāgaraś cāpi dustaraḥ
english: "What plan do you all consider best for crossing the ocean? This army is great, and the ocean is difficult to cross."

sanskrit: tatrānye vyāharanti sma vānarāḥ paṭumāninaḥ samarthā laṅghane sindhor na tu kṛtsnasya vānarāḥ
english: Some monkeys who thought themselves clever spoke up there saying that some monkeys were capable of leaping across the ocean, but not all.

sanskrit: ke cin naubhir vyavasyanti kecīc ca vividhaiḥ plavaiḥ neti rāmaś ca tān sarvān sāntvayan pratyabhāṣata
english: Some proposed boats, others various kinds of rafts. Rāma pacified them all and replied, "No" —

sanskrit: śatayojanavistāraṃ na śaktāḥ sarvavānarāḥ krāntuṃ toyanidhiṃ vīrā naiṣā vo naiṣṭhikī matiḥ
english: "Not all the monkeys are capable of crossing this sea, a hundred yojanas wide, O heroes. That is not the final plan for you."

sanskrit: nāvo na santi senāyā bahvyas tārayituṃ tathā vaṇijām upaghātaṃ ca katham asmadvidhaś caret
english: "There are not enough ships to ferry this whole army, and how could one like us bring harm to merchants? That is not acceptable."

sanskrit: vistīrṇaṃ caiva naḥ sainyaṃ hanyāc chidreṣu vai paraḥ plavoḍupapratāraś ca naivātra mama rocate
english: "Our army is spread wide, and the enemy would strike at gaps. Crossing by rafts or boats does not please me here."

sanskrit: ahaṃ tv imaṃ jalanidhiṃ samārapsyāmy upāyataḥ pratiśeṣyāmy upavasan darśayiṣyati māṃ tataḥ
english: "I shall address this ocean through means — I will lie in fast, and it will then reveal itself to me."

sanskrit: na ced darśayitā mārgaṃ dhakṣyāmy enam ahaṃ tataḥ mahāstrair apratihatair atyagnipavanojjvalaiḥ
english: "If it will not show me a way, I shall then burn it up with my irresistible great weapons, blazing more fiercely than fire and wind."

sanskrit: ity uktvā sahasaumitrir upaspṛśyātha rāghavaḥ pratiśiśye jalanidhiṃ vidhivat kuśasaṃstare
english: Having spoken thus, Rāghava, together with Lakṣmaṇa, sipped water and ritually lay down on a bed of kusa grass facing the ocean.

sanskrit: sāgaras tu tataḥ svapne darśayām āsa rāghavam devo nadanadībhartā śrīmān yādogaṇair vṛtaḥ
english: Then the ocean, lord of rivers and streams, the god surrounded by hosts of aquatic creatures, appeared to Rāghava in a dream.

sanskrit: kausalyāmātar ity evam ābhāṣya madhuraṃ vacaḥ idam ity āha ratnānām ākaraiḥ śataśo vṛtaḥ
english: Addressing him sweetly as "Son of Kausalyā," and surrounded by hundreds of treasure-mines, the ocean spoke thus:

sanskrit: brūhi kiṃ te karomy atra sāhāyyaṃ puruṣarṣabha ikṣvākur asmi te jñātir iti rāmas tam abravīt
english: "Tell me, what assistance shall I render you here, O bull among men?" And Rāma replied, "I am of the Ikṣvāku lineage; you are my kinsman."

sanskrit: mārgam icchāmi sainyasya dattaṃ nadanadīpate yena gatvā daśagrīvaṃ hanyāṃ paulastyapāṃsanam
english: "I desire a path granted for my army, O lord of rivers and streams, by which I may go and slay the ten-headed one, Rāvaṇa, disgrace of the Pulastyas."

sanskrit: yady evaṃ yācato mārgaṃ na pradāsyati me bhavān śarais tvāṃ śoṣayiṣyāmi divyāstrapratimantritaiḥ
english: "If you do not grant the path I thus beseech, I shall dry you up with arrows charged with divine weapon-spells."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ bruvataḥ śrutvā rāmasya varuṇālayaḥ uvāca vyathito vākyam iti baddhāñjaliḥ sthitaḥ
english: Hearing Rāma speak thus, the abode of Varuṇa, greatly distressed, stood with folded hands and spoke these words:

sanskrit: necchāmi pratighātaṃ te nāsmi vighnakaras tava śṛṇu cedaṃ vaco rāma śrutvā kartavyam ācara
english: "I do not wish to oppose you; I am not an obstacle to you. Hear this word, O Rāma, and having heard it, act accordingly."

sanskrit: yadi dāsyāmi te mārgaṃ sainyasya vrajato ''jñayā anye 'py ājñāpayiṣyanti mām evaṃ dhanuṣo balāt
english: "If I give your army a path by command, others too will command me thus by the force of their bows."

sanskrit: asti tv atra nalo nāma vānaraḥ śilpisaṃmataḥ tvaṣṭur devasya tanayo balavān viśvakarmaṇaḥ
english: "There is, however, a monkey named Nala here, regarded as a craftsman, the mighty son of the divine Tvaṣṭṛ, Viśvakarman."

sanskrit: sa yat kāṣṭhaṃ tṛṇaṃ vāpi śilāṃ vā kṣepsyate mayi sarvaṃ tad dhārayiṣyāmi sa te setur bhaviṣyati
english: "Whatever wood, grass, or rock he casts upon me, I shall bear all of it — it will become a bridge for you."

sanskrit: ity uktvāntarhite tasmin rāmo nalam uvāca ha kuru setuṃ samudre tvaṃ śakto hy asi mato mama
english: When that one had spoken and disappeared, Rāma said to Nala: "Build a bridge across the ocean — you are capable of it in my judgment."

sanskrit: tenopāyena kākutsthaḥ setubandham akārayat daśayojanavistāram āyataṃ śatayojanam
english: By that means, the descendant of Kākutstha had the bridge built — ten yojanas wide and a hundred yojanas long.

sanskrit: nalasetur iti khyāto yo 'dyāpi prathito bhuvi rāmasyājñāṃ puraskṛtya dhāryate girisaṃnibhaḥ
english: Known as "Nala's bridge," it is still renowned on earth even today, mountain-like, maintained under Rāma's command.

sanskrit: tatrasthaṃ sa tu dharmātmā samāgacchad vibhīṣaṇaḥ bhrātā vai rākṣasendrasya caturbhiḥ sacivaiḥ saha
english: Then righteous Vibhīṣaṇa, brother of the king of the rakshasas, came to him there with four ministers.

sanskrit: pratijagrāha rāmas taṃ svāgatena mahāmanāḥ sugrīvasya tu śaṅkābhūt praṇidhiḥ syād iti sma ha
english: The magnanimous Rāma received him with a welcome. But Sugrīva was suspicious, thinking he might be a spy.

sanskrit: rāghavas tasya ceṣṭābhiḥ samyak ca cariteṅgitaiḥ yadā tattvena tuṣṭo 'bhūt tata enam apūjayat
english: When Rāghava was truly satisfied by Vibhīṣaṇa's conduct, behavior, and deportment, he then honored him.

sanskrit: sarvarākṣasarājye cāpy abhyaṣiñcad vibhīṣaṇam cakre ca mantrānucaraṃ suhṛdaṃ lakṣmaṇasya ca
english: He anointed Vibhīṣaṇa as king over all the realm of the rakshasas, and made him a counselor-companion and friend of Lakṣmaṇa.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇamate caiva so 'tyakrāman mahārṇavam sasainyaḥ setunā tena māsenaiva narādhipa
english: And on Vibhīṣaṇa's advice, he crossed the great ocean with his army by that bridge — in just one month, O lord of men.

sanskrit: tato gatvā samāsādya laṅkodyānāny anekaśaḥ bhedayām āsa kapibhir mahānti ca bahūni ca
english: Then, having gone and reached Laṅkā, he had the many great gardens of Laṅkā broken and destroyed by the monkeys.

sanskrit: tatrāstāṃ rāvaṇāmātyau rākṣasau śukasāraṇau cārau vānararūpeṇa tau jagrāha vibhīṣaṇaḥ
english: There were two rakshasa ministers of Rāvaṇa, Śuka and Sāraṇa, who had taken monkey form as spies — Vibhīṣaṇa caught them.

sanskrit: pratipannau yadā rūpaṃ rākṣasaṃ tau niśācarau darśayitvā tataḥ sainyaṃ rāmaḥ paścād avāsṛjat
english: When those two night-rangers had reverted to their rakshasa forms and shown themselves, Rāma thereafter released them after showing the army.

sanskrit: niveśyopavane sainyaṃ tac chūraḥ prājñavānaram preṣayām āsa dautyena rāvaṇasya tato 'ṅgadam
english: Having settled the army in the grove, that heroic one then sent the wise monkey Aṅgada as an emissary to Rāvaṇa.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca prabhūtānnodake tasmin bahumūlaphale vane senāṃ niveśya kākutstho vidhivat paryarakṣata
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having settled the army in that forest abounding in food, water, roots, and fruits, the descendant of Kākutstha duly kept guard.

sanskrit: rāvaṇaś ca vidhiṃ cakre laṅkāyāṃ śāstranirmitam prakṛtyaiva durādharṣā dṛḍhaprākāratoraṇā
english: And Rāvaṇa made the prescribed arrangements in Laṅkā as ordained by the scriptures. By its very nature Laṅkā was hard to assail, with sturdy ramparts and gateways.

sanskrit: agādhatoyāḥ parikhā mīnanakrasamākulāḥ babhūvuḥ sapta durdharṣāḥ khādiraiḥ śaṅkubhiś citāḥ
english: There were seven moats, fathomless in water, swarming with fish and crocodiles, difficult to overcome, studded with stakes of khadira wood.

sanskrit: karṇāṭṭayantradurdharṣā babhūvuḥ sahuḍopalāḥ sāśīviṣaghaṭāyodhāḥ sasarjarasapāṃsavaḥ
english: The battlements were formidable with their machines and projecting cornices, with sharp-edged stones, fighters with pots of venomous serpents, and dust mixed with poisonous resin.

sanskrit: musalālātanārācatomarāsiparaśvadhaiḥ anvitāś ca śataghnībhiḥ samadhūcchiṭamudgarāḥ
english: They were furnished with pestles, firebrands, nārācas, tomaras, swords, axes, sataghnīs, and clubs smeared with pitch.

sanskrit: puradvāreṣu sarveṣu gulmāḥ sthāvarajaṅgamāḥ babhūvuḥ pattibahulāḥ prabhūtagajavājinaḥ
english: At every city gate there were stationary and mobile guard-posts, with abundant infantry, elephants, and horses.

sanskrit: aṅgadas tv atha laṅkāyā dvāradeśam upāgataḥ vidito rākṣasendrasya praviveśa gatavyathaḥ
english: Then Aṅgada approached the gateway of Laṅkā, made himself known to the king of the rakshasas, and entered fearlessly.

sanskrit: madhye rākṣasakoṭīnāṃ bahvīnāṃ sumahābalaḥ śuśubhe meghamālābhir āditya iva saṃvṛtaḥ
english: Of immense strength, in the midst of many crores of rakshasas, he shone like the sun surrounded by rows of clouds.

sanskrit: sa samāsādya paulastyam amātyair abhisaṃvṛtam rāmasaṃdeśam āmantrya vāgmī vaktuṃ pracakrame
english: Approaching Rāvaṇa, son of Paulastya, surrounded by his ministers, and announcing Rāma's message, the eloquent one began to speak.

sanskrit: āha tvāṃ rāghavo rājan kosalendro mahāyaśāḥ prāptakālam idaṃ vākyaṃ tad ādatsva kuruṣva ca
english: "O king, Rāghava, lord of Kosala, of great renown, says this timely message to you — receive it and act upon it:

sanskrit: akṛtātmānam āsādya rājānam anaye ratam vinaśyanty anayāviṣṭā deśāś ca nagarāṇi ca
english: 'When they encounter a king of uncontrolled self who revels in wrongdoing, lands and cities possessed by that wrongdoing perish.'

sanskrit: tvayaikenāparāddhaṃ me sītām āharatā balāt vadhāyānaparāddhānām anyeṣāṃ tad bhaviṣyati
english: 'You alone have wronged me by forcibly abducting Sītā — yet this will bring about the killing of others who have not wronged me.'

sanskrit: ye tvayā baladarpābhyām āviṣṭena vanecarāḥ ṛṣayo hiṃsitāḥ pūrvaṃ devāś cāpy avamānitāḥ
english: 'The forest-dwellers and sages who were harmed by you, seized by arrogance and pride of strength, and the gods too who were dishonored —'

sanskrit: rājarṣayaś ca nihatā rudantyaś cāhṛtāḥ striyaḥ tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ phalaṃ tasyānayasya te
english: '— and the royal sages who were slain, and the weeping women who were carried off — this fruit of that wrongdoing of yours has now arrived.'

sanskrit: hantāsmi tvāṃ sahāmātyaṃ yudhyasva puruṣo bhava paśya me dhanuṣo vīryaṃ mānuṣasya niśācara
english: 'I shall slay you along with your ministers. Fight — be a man! Behold the power of my bow, O night-ranger, though I am but human.'

sanskrit: mucyatāṃ jānakī sītā na me mokṣyasi karhi cit arākṣasam imaṃ lokaṃ kartāsmi niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: 'Let Jānakī Sītā be released. You shall never escape from me. I shall make this world free of rakshasas with my sharpened arrows.'

sanskrit: iti tasya bruvāṇasya dūtasya paruṣaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā na mamṛṣe rājā rāvaṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ
english: Hearing those harsh words of the messenger as he spoke thus, king Rāvaṇa, overcome with rage, did not endure them.

sanskrit: iṅgitajñās tato bhartuś catvāro rajanīcarāḥ caturṣv aṅgeṣu jagṛhuḥ śārdūlam iva pakṣiṇaḥ
english: Then four night-rangers, skilled in reading their master's signs, seized him at four limbs, as birds would seize a tiger.

sanskrit: tāṃs tathāṅgeṣu saṃsaktān aṅgado rajanīcarān ādāyaiva kham utpatya prāsādatalam āviśat
english: Aṅgada, taking those night-rangers as they clung to his limbs, leapt into the sky and landed on the roof of the palace.

sanskrit: vegenotpatatas tasya petus te rajanīcarāḥ bhuvi saṃbhinnahṛdayāḥ prahāraparipīḍitāḥ
english: As he flew up with great speed, those night-rangers fell to the ground with crushed hearts, tormented by his blows.

sanskrit: sa mukto harmyaśikharāt tasmāt punar avāpatat laṅghayitvā purīṃ laṅkāṃ svabalasya samīpataḥ
english: Freed from that palace roof, he leapt again, cleared the city of Laṅkā entirely, and landed near his own army.

sanskrit: kosalendram athābhyetya sarvam āvedya cāṅgadaḥ viśaśrāma sa tejasvī rāghaveṇābhinanditaḥ
english: Then, having gone to the lord of Kosala and reported everything, that glorious Aṅgada rested, honored by Rāghava.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarvābhisāreṇa harīṇāṃ vātaraṃhasām bhedayām āsa laṅkāyāḥ prākāraṃ raghunandanaḥ
english: Then the delight of the Raghu line, with the full assault of the wind-swift monkeys, broke through the rampart of Laṅkā.

sanskrit: vibhīṣaṇarkṣādhipatī puraskṛtyātha lakṣmaṇaḥ dakṣiṇaṃ nagaradvāram avāmṛdnād durāsadam
english: And Lakṣmaṇa, placing Vibhīṣaṇa and the lord of bears at the front, crushed the southern city gate, which was hard to assail.

sanskrit: karabhāruṇagātrāṇāṃ harīṇāṃ yuddhaśālinām koṭīśatasahasreṇa laṅkām abhyapatat tadā
english: Then a hundred thousand crore of battle-skilled monkeys with reddish-brown limbs like elephant trunks attacked Laṅkā.

sanskrit: utpatadbhiḥ patadbhiś ca nipatadbhiś ca vānaraiḥ nādṛśyata tadā sūryo rajasā nāśitaprabhaḥ
english: With monkeys leaping up, falling down, and swooping, the sun could not be seen at that time — its radiance destroyed by the dust.

sanskrit: śāliprasūnasadṛśaiḥ śirīṣakusumaprabhaiḥ taruṇādityasadṛśaiḥ śaragauraiś ca vānaraiḥ
english: With monkeys resembling rice-blossoms, shining like shirisha flowers, like the young sun, and fair as autumn reeds —

sanskrit: prākāraṃ dadṛśus te tu samantāt kapilīkṛtam rākṣasā vismitā rājan sastrīvṛddhāḥ samantataḥ
english: — the rakshasas, O king, along with their women and elders, marveled to see the rampart turned tawny on all sides.
